targets.evidence_quote: MacKuen, Erikson, and Stimson (1989, 1992) argue that the aggregate distribution of party identification, or macropartisanship, shifts significantly over short periods in response to changes in presidential popularity and consumer sentiment. We replicate this analysis using a more extensive inventory of Gallup and CBS/New York Timesdata and find considerably less evidence of partisan fluctuation.
targets.outcome_quote: The amount of partisan change caused by short-term movements in consumer sentiment and presidential popularity is found to be two to three times smaller than initially reported by MacKuen et al. (1989). Our results indicate that macropartisanship adjusts to short-term shocks in a limited and gradual fashion, consistent with traditional views of partisan realignment.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract describes both cited originals as reporting responsiveness to these inputs and reports responsiveness in the same direction but smaller. Reduced magnitude alone does not imply mixed. Full-text verdict and reference entries unavailable.
